budget.metric: relative error of the simulated thermal Z displacement of the tool relative to the table at the measured times (curve points) and of its plateau value, from a cold start at the case's speed
budget.note: Set after a first run of the spindle_growth harness had been seen (first-round report); justified only by the evidence below. One machine running the same speed program reaches plateau Z errors that differ by up to +-33 % of their mean when only the workshop ambient changes (Wei 2023: 17.7-34.8 um at 2000 rpm, 35.0-49.5 um at 4000 rpm, 46.1-58.2 um at 6000 rpm, computed here from the case values), and an air-conditioning event changes a run from 21 to 60 um (Yang 2024). The measured Z is the whole tool-to-table loop (shaft growth plus headstock and column), which a spindle-body model only partly contains. A thermal model with the machine's own heat sources and conductances can hold the plateau to about the ambient-band spread; 30 % is that bound and still separates a calibrated model from defaults that miss by a factor of several.
